recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Any future change to make Claim.use optional again or to mark use/type/subType as modifiers should come from a new explicit FM work-group decision rather than from reapplying superseded parts of FHIR-15788.
issue_request: FHIR-15788 was Published/Persuasive with Modification for STU3 Financial Management. It asked why Claim.use was not mandatory, why it was not a modifier, and why the use codes were not business terms such as claim, preauthorization, and predetermination.
initial_application: Tracker commit ec9fb5cdae40510dbcb39ff2c380ea2f10b920fb applied FHIR-15788 across Claim, ClaimResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit spreadsheets. Commit 63cb7bfb7b45cb980bea6f56c061b764bd02a5f7 immediately removed the .use Is-Modifier flag after Jira comments questioned modifier status, and 10ac2496c7fa29fe458c13a1ef3f7edb89485acc performed further FHIR-15788-related FM cleanup. The later StructureDefinition source migration preserved the business use codes and non-modifier shape.
additional_context: Claim, ClaimResponse, and ExplanationOfBenefit are active FM build resources. Current source marks status as the modifier element, while use, type, and subType are not modifiers. The use elements are 1..1 and bind to claim-use values claim, preauthorization, and predetermination. Later Published/Persuasive FHIR-19457 explicitly requested Claim.use at 1..1 and is already reconciled on the combined branch; FHIR-36101 later resolved no-change on splitting Claim/ClaimResponse preauthorization and predetermination use cases into separate resources.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No source edit is needed because the current source already contains the required business codes, preserves the immediate undo of the modifier change, and reflects the later Claim.use cardinality decision.

related_jiras.note: Later Published/Persuasive Claim issue explicitly requested Claim.use at 1..1, superseding FHIR-15788's optionality discussion for current source.
Later Resolved - No Change issue kept Claim and ClaimResponse scope covering claim, preauthorization, and predetermination rather than splitting those uses into separate resources.
Adjacent EOB purpose documentation issue concerns the same claim-use value family and is already represented on the combined branch.
